name: @veilio-inc/mcp

tools.name: anonymize_file
tools.description: Read a file from disk and return it with every proprietary identifier replaced by a placeholder (__CLS__1, __FN__2, …) and every credential irreversibly redacted. PREFER THIS over anonymize_text: Veilio reads the file itself, so the real identifiers never enter your context — you only ever see the masked form. Use it before reasoning about, quoting, or forwarding proprietary source. The symbol map is stored locally so restore_text can reverse it later.

path.description: File path, relative to the project root.

language.description: Source language. "auto" (default) detects it. Supported: TypeScript / JavaScript, Python, Go, Java / Kotlin, C#, Rust, Ruby, PHP, C / C++, SQL.

preamble.description: Prepend a note explaining the placeholders, for forwarding to another model.

tools.name: anonymize_text
tools.description: Mask identifiers and redact credentials in text passed as an argument. Only use this for text you ALREADY hold — something the user pasted into the conversation. If the content is in a file, use anonymize_file instead: passing file contents through this tool means the real identifiers are already in your context, which defeats the purpose.

language.description: Source language. "auto" (default) detects it. Supported: TypeScript / JavaScript, Python, Go, Java / Kotlin, C#, Rust, Ruby, PHP, C / C++, SQL.

tools.name: restore_text
tools.description: Swap placeholders back to the real identifiers using the stored symbol map, and strip AI-generated noise (JSDoc, TODO comments, narration). Its result puts the real names into your context, which undoes the masking for whatever it restores: call it only when the developer asks for restored text for their own use, never to read the project. Irreversibly redacted credentials stay redacted - that is deliberate.

strict.description: Refuse instead of returning text that still holds a placeholder (invented, altered, disputed, or the team's maps unreadable) or a redaction, which cannot be restored: an error naming them, and no text.

tools.name: scan_secrets
tools.description: Detect credentials — API keys, tokens, private keys, connection-string passwords, emails, private IPs — without modifying anything and WITHOUT putting the values in your context (findings carry truncated previews only). Run this on a file before reading it, or on a diff before committing.

path.description: File to scan, relative to the project root.

text.description: Text to scan, if not reading a file.

tools.name: symbol_map_summary
tools.description: Report how many placeholders exist and which kinds. Deliberately returns placeholder KEYS only, never the real names — so you can reason about coverage without de-anonymizing anything.

instructions: Use anonymize_file before reasoning about proprietary source: it reads the file itself and returns only masked code. It does not stop the agent reading files with its own tools, and what those read reaches you as written: with a coding agent, use the guard (veilio-guard, Claude Code), or turn off the agent's own file and shell tools so this server is the only way to the code. Use scan_secrets to check a file or diff for credentials without seeing their values. restore_text puts the real names into your context: use it only when the developer asks for restored text for their own use. this agent has no Veilio guard yet. Turn off its own file and shell tools so this server is the only way to your code; otherwise its reads reach the model as written.
